control-structure: STPA step 2 for this project's own workflow, COMPUTED from the authored measures (Sensor and Feedback items - the mechanism, its determinism and the loop it closes), the hook config, git hooks, workflow files, CLI facts and declared deciders (D0284). Actuators and responsibilities are derived from the actions; process models and the other inputs/outputs (the handbook's fifth element type, D0363) are authored and joined onto the roles; the step-2 gate is decided clause by clause from this structure; the remote's rules are fetched live and never copied.

actions.name: workflowCi
actions.title: ci.yml: fail the build
actions.data: steps: clippy (-D warnings) | test | keel gates (kernel-free backstop — SKIP_VALIDATE can't bypass CI) | script probes (every scripts/*.py that ships known cases, run as a gate; D0394) | keel audit-history (tree-derived verdicts over the pushed range) | keel adoption-check (a unit must land in a project that lacks it) | keel audit-adherence (guard-set monotonicity — a control cannot be disarmed unsigned, D0209) | keel audit-ci-runs (the external-fact gate — a ci-run receipt names a real green run on the judged SHA, D0323); runs: keel validate, keel guard, keel check-engine, keel rules, keel audit-history, keel adoption-check, keel audit-adherence, keel audit-ci-runs

actions.name: workflowCurrency
actions.title: currency.yml: fail the build
actions.data: steps: is D0338 accepted? (D0337 - the schedule is inert until the human's word) | build | currency pass (pull as verbatim Statements, library sync, drift; one report) | gate, then commit the new Statements (words only - nothing is triaged); runs: keel currency, keel gate

actions.name: workflowRelease
actions.title: release.yml: fail the build
actions.data: steps: clippy (deny warnings) | cargo test | keel gate (validate + guards) | build keel (release) | stage binary (unix) | stage binary (windows) | checksum (unix) | checksum (windows) | attach to GitHub Release | aggregate and verify; runs: keel gate, keel validate, keel guard

actuators.name: actHarnessVerdict
actuators.title: Claude Code applies the hook's verdict
actuators.mechanism: the harness reads the hook's stdout JSON and blocks, denies or allows the tool call or the turn; the hook itself changes nothing

actuators.name: actLaunchSettings
actuators.title: the launch passes settings above project scope
actuators.mechanism: `keel claude` passes --settings and --plugin-dir; the harness's own precedence carries the pin, so a kill switch on disk is overridden (D0296 run 6)

actuators.name: actGitHookDispatch
actuators.title: git runs the hook and honours its exit code
actuators.mechanism: core.hooksPath -> .githooks/<hook>; a non-zero exit refuses the commit or the push - git carries the refusal, keel only exits

actuators.name: actCheckConclusion
actuators.title: the runner records the job's conclusion on the ref
actuators.mechanism: GitHub Actions executes the job; the red or green conclusion is all the action leaves on main - preventive only if branch protection requires it (see remote.reading)

actuators.name: actWriteLayer
actuators.title: the keel write layer lands the file
actuators.mechanism: temp-file-then-rename under .keel-write-lock; actor and date required or the write refuses (D0129, issue184/185)

actuators.name: actSurfaceRewrite
actuators.title: keel rewrites the generated surface in place
actuators.mechanism: init, migrate, sync-claude, activate and deactivate write the engine-owned files directly; sync-claude --check reports the drift afterwards

actuators.name: actGitPush
actuators.title: git pushes after the gate
actuators.mechanism: keel sync / keel land gate every project in the workspace, then git pushes; what the ref accepts is the remote's rule

actuators.name: actAgentRouting
actuators.title: the agent reads the direction and routes the turn
actuators.mechanism: prose enters the agent's context; the intake skill and the agent's own routing translate it - nothing mechanical carries it, and the routing rig investigates whether it arrives (D0382, issue415)

actuators.name: actServeWriteApi
actuators.title: keel serve calls the write API
actuators.mechanism: HTTP on 127.0.0.1:7777 into the same write layer; a tap is signed by the paired device (D0334/D0335) and an unsigned one writes nothing

actuators.name: actHarnessFileTools
actuators.title: the harness's Write, Edit and Bash tools change the source
actuators.mechanism: keel mediates none of it: pre-write advises on protected surfaces, and manifest drift makes done work suspect afterwards

actuators.name: actRefUpdateRefusal
actuators.title: GitHub refuses the ref update
actuators.mechanism: branch protection is evaluated at receive-pack: a force-push or a deletion is rejected before the ref moves

processModels.name: pmAgent
processModels.beliefs: That the ready list is the priority (true, D0052); that a green Stop gate ends the turn honestly (true for FORM); that its own judgment on demo/inspect/analyze suffices as verification (the belief st065 withdraws); that a non-fork classification is its call (true, and the channel acts on it).

processModels.name: pmCI
processModels.beliefs: That the pushed range is the whole story (true - audit-history walks it); that its verdict is read (false often enough to have a Decision, D0266); that its pinned binary is the engine under test (true here, where it builds from source).

processModels.name: pmCommitGate
processModels.beliefs: That the staged tree is the tree being committed (true - it gates the index, not the working copy); that the binary core.hooksPath resolved is the pinned engine (true only through the probe, D0343/GH#55 - PATH used to decide it); that HEAD after the commit is the SHA its results will be judged against (false whenever the post-commit land merges first); that a green fast tier means the model is honestly formed, never that the work is complete (D0098).

processModels.name: pmConsole
processModels.beliefs: That a tap signed by the paired device is the human's judgment (true as far as a device can prove - D0334/D0335 bind the device, not the person); that the working tree it serves is the tree the agent's session sees (true - and the reason its writes must be diffed out of the agent's commit); that the queue it renders is the whole set awaiting the human (true - authority-queue is the same lens the brief reads).

processModels.name: pmHooks
processModels.beliefs: That the session is an agent session because the environment says so (agent-mutable); that the binary they resolve is the pinned one (true only where KEEL_BIN or PATH agrees with the pin - issue 43 downstream); that a clean fast tier means the edit was safe to continue (form only).

processModels.name: pmHuman
processModels.beliefs: That an auto-accepted Decision is fine unless overridden; that a green gate means the model is honest (true) and the work is complete (false by design, D0098); that the DoD verified is the DoD agreed (FALSE today - issue343: the owner may rewrite it after the pass); that a pass with a receipt was produced by what the receipt names (unchecked - CI does not re-run receipts).

processModels.name: pmRemote
processModels.beliefs: That whoever holds the push credential is the actor named in the commit (false - the credential is a machine's, the commit's author field is prose); that a ref update is safe when it is a fast-forward (true for history, silent about content - it reads no gate); that a required status check is what makes CI preventive (true, and none is required here, so CI is detective - remote.reading).

otherInputsOutputs.name: oioDecisionBrief
otherInputsOutputs.title: the published decision brief
otherInputsOutputs.externalParty: the claude.ai artifact host - the one page the pending set is published to (D0359), read outside every control here

otherInputsOutputs.name: oioGithubIssues
otherInputsOutputs.title: issues filed on the repository
otherInputsOutputs.externalParty: anyone who can open an issue - an unauthenticated stranger when the repository is public, which is why D0264 routes by visibility

otherInputsOutputs.name: oioHooksPathConfig
otherInputsOutputs.title: core.hooksPath and the resolved binary
otherInputsOutputs.externalParty: the machine's git config - machine-local, uncommitted, and the whole reason the commit gate runs at all; a clone without it commits ungated

otherInputsOutputs.name: oioHostClock
otherInputsOutputs.title: the host clock and file mtimes
otherInputsOutputs.externalParty: the operating system - the guard receipt is keyed on mtimes and refuses a path younger than two seconds (D0371), and every judgedAt is the host's date

otherInputsOutputs.name: oioModelApi
otherInputsOutputs.title: the model's completions
otherInputsOutputs.externalParty: the Anthropic API - the agent's every judgment is a sample from it (issue392: two of four verdicts flipped on identical inputs)

otherInputsOutputs.name: oioPairedDeviceKey
otherInputsOutputs.title: the paired device's key
otherInputsOutputs.externalParty: the browser that paired with the code the serving terminal printed (D0334) - a device, and whoever holds it

otherInputsOutputs.name: oioPushCredential
otherInputsOutputs.title: the push credential
otherInputsOutputs.externalParty: the machine's credential helper - the remote authenticates a token, and the token belongs to a machine both the human and the agent push from

otherInputsOutputs.name: oioReleaseBinary
otherInputsOutputs.title: the released binary
otherInputsOutputs.externalParty: downstream projects - keelw and keel init fetch the release asset the tag names, and a defect here becomes theirs (D0275, D0302)

otherInputsOutputs.name: oioSessionEnvironment
otherInputsOutputs.title: the harness's session environment
otherInputsOutputs.externalParty: Claude Code - the hook event payload, KEEL_BIN, PATH and the settings precedence decide which binary fires and whether it fires at all (D0296, GH#43)

otherInputsOutputs.name: oioToolchain
otherInputsOutputs.title: the runner image and the Rust toolchain
otherInputsOutputs.externalParty: GitHub-hosted runners, rustup and crates.io - CI builds the engine under test from source on whatever they serve that day

otherInputsOutputs.name: oioUncommittedEdits
otherInputsOutputs.title: out-of-band edits to the working tree
otherInputsOutputs.externalParty: an editor, the console, or a second session writing the same working tree - they reach the model through no keel command and no hook sees them (S-F9)

remote.reading: CI is DETECTIVE: no status check is required, so a red build reports a commit already on main

stepTwoGate.clause: at least one controller, one control action and one controlled process
every arrow is labelled functionally with what passes (no bare Command / Status / Computer)
stepTwoGate.evidence: 49 actions and 100 feedback paths carry a title and data; bare: none

stepTwoGate.clause: every controlled process has at least one controller acting on it
stepTwoGate.evidence: acted on: model, main-ref, enforcement-surface, deliverable, work, agent-turn; with no controller: none

stepTwoGate.clause: responsibilities are traced: every acting controller answers for a hazard on a process it reaches, and every hazard has a controller that answers for it
stepTwoGate.evidence: 31 responsibilities over 9 hazards; controllers with none: none; hazards nobody answers for: none

stepTwoGate.clause: every controller has a process model, or its absence is justified
stepTwoGate.evidence: 7 process models for 7 present controllers; without one: none

stepTwoGate.clause: each process model is maintained by feedback, or by an other-input, reaching its controller
the fifth element type - other inputs and outputs, neither control nor feedback - is enumerated or declared empty with a reason
stepTwoGate.evidence: 9 inbound, 2 outbound, each with its external party

stepTwoGate.clause: sensors and actuators are present or deliberately deferred to step 4
stepTwoGate.evidence: 21 sensors authored, 11 actuators computed from the actions
